title: fix(objectql): a runAs:'user' hook sees its organization's members in sys_user, as the user's own request does
body:
Fixes #24497
Clause-②: no (a runtime producer fix: a `runAs: 'user'` hook reads what the same user's own request reads. Nothing `@objectstack/spec` declares moves; owes the seat's review of record before the queue)

## What was wrong

`ScopedContext.withRunAs('user')` pins a hook's `ctx.api` to `{ ...triggering context, isSystem: false }` and seeds nothing. A hook fired from a hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId, tenantId }` context therefore carried no `org_user_ids`. The `sys_user_org_members` policy (`id in current_user.org_user_ids`) compiled `unresolved-variable` and dropped out, so the hook saw the acting user's own `sys_user` row only. The same user's request saw their organisation's members too. This is the hook-side twin of #24448 (PR #24495), and a precondition of #24341: under its one-policy `sys_user` default, such a hook would lose its own row as well.

## Measurement (real stack, before and after)

The probe is `packages/services/service-automation/src/runas-user-hook-org-peers.integration.test.ts`. It boots ObjectKernel, ObjectQLPlugin, driver-sql on better-sqlite3 `:memory:`, the identity objects (`createIdentityObjectsPlugin`) and the real SecurityPlugin with its shipped default permission sets. A `runAs: 'user'` hook on `hook_probe`'s `afterInsert` reads `sys_user` through `ctx.api`, and a middleware records the context that read carries.

Fixture: organisation A (the Default Organization) and organisation B. `usr_me` belongs to A and B and acts in A. `usr_peer` belongs to A. `usr_other` belongs to B only. `usr_loner` belongs to none.

The probe was committed alone first (`1f1afac08`) and run against unchanged `origin/main` `666283aea`. The after column is head `e82725a18`.

| triggering context | before: rows / hook context | after: rows / hook context |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{ isSystem: true, userId: usr_me, tenantId: A }` (the card's shape) | `usr_me` / no positions, no permissions, no `org_user_ids` | `usr_me, usr_peer` / positions `org_member, everyone`, permissions `member_default`, `org_user_ids` `usr_me, usr_peer` |
| the request-resolved envelope (control) | `usr_me, usr_peer` / envelope verbatim | `usr_me, usr_peer` / envelope verbatim, nothing resolved |
| approvals' exact envelope `{ isSystem: true, positions: [], permissions: [], userId: usr_me }` | `usr_me` / `org_user_ids` absent (read from the ablation leg) | `usr_me` / `org_user_ids` `usr_me`, positions and permissions `[]` verbatim |
| no organisation `{ isSystem: true, userId: usr_me }` | `usr_me` | `usr_me` / `org_user_ids` `usr_me` |

`usr_other` and `usr_loner` are never in any answer. The CONTROL case, the user's own request acting in A, answers `usr_me, usr_peer` on both trees.

The probe does not fire through `plugin-approvals`' real write path. No package composes approvals, the SecurityPlugin and the identity objects in its dev dependencies. `plugin-approvals` lacks `plugin-security` and `plugin-auth`; `service-automation` and `runtime` lack `plugin-approvals`; `qa/dogfood` and `cli` have all three but boot the full app. Adding a dev dependency would move the lockfile outside this card's fence. So the probe fires from the approvals' exact envelope, copied from `SYSTEM_CTX` in `approval-service.ts` and `approval-node.ts`.

## The change

- **`ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]()` (`engine.ts`, the `ScopedContext` class)**, keyed on a symbol declared in `hook-run-as.ts` and not exported from the package entry, is an async method, the second half of the `'user'` derivation. It applies #24495's run-setup rule to the hook's pinned context:
  - Seeding uses `resolveUserAuthzGrants` (`@objectstack/core`), the resolver the request path seeds through. There is no second resolver and no second definition of "peer".
  - A context with no `permissions` takes the resolved positions and permission sets.
  - Positions and permission sets the context already carries stay verbatim, and only the peer list is taken, so a narrowed ceiling is never re-broadened.
  - A context that already carries `org_user_ids` resolves nothing.
  - It reads no elevation flag: it runs only on the api `withRunAs('user')` produced.
- **`seedHookUserGrants` (`hook-run-as.ts`)** is the step the wrapper awaits after `deriveHookApi`. An api that cannot seed, such as the refusing `UnscopedHookApi`, is returned as is.
- **`installRunAsApi` (`hook-wrappers.ts`)** is now async for `'user'` only.
  - `'inherit'` takes no extra `await` and keeps the engine-built api by reference.
  - `'system'` installs `sudo()` as before.
  - The `UnscopedHookApi` refusal (no `userId`) does not move.
  - When the resolver fails (an unreadable permission store), the hook keeps the unseeded pin and one `warn` names the consequence. This is narrower, never elevated, and the same posture as the flow run setup.

**Why `withRunAs` stays synchronous.** `runtime`'s stored-metadata seams (`deriveThroughSeam`) wrap `withRunAs`'s return value synchronously. A Promise there would hand back an unwrapped api, which is a route around the seam. So the async half is a separate method, reached by the wrapper while `ctx.api` is still the engine-built `ScopedContext`. The sandbox body layers wrap it later, at handler time.

**Cost.** A `runAs: 'user'` hook whose triggering context lacks `permissions` or `org_user_ids` pays one `resolveUserAuthzGrants` per dispatch: one wave of five concurrent reads, plus the permission-set reads the resolver makes. A request-resolved context carries both and pays nothing. The request-grants memo does not apply here, because it is open only inside `resolveAuthzContext`. The #11971 grants cache answers it when `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` is enabled; it is off by default. A hook is request-shaped, so it is not added to the cache's ruled bypass list.

**Where the files landed vs the claim's fence.** The three source files are in the fence. Outside it:
- `engine.ts` gains one import line for `resolveUserAuthzGrants` beside its existing `@objectstack/core` imports. That is not PR #24508's predicate region.
- The real-stack probe lives in `service-automation`, beside its flow twin. That package is the one whose dev dependencies already compose the whole stack; `objectql` cannot depend on driver-sql, plugin-auth or plugin-security.

## Pins

- `hook-run-as.test.ts`, new `[#24497]` block (layer 1, a real `ScopedContext` over a recording engine that answers the resolver's reads). It covers:
  - the hand-built shape carries the organisation's peers and nothing beyond;
  - carried positions and permission sets stay verbatim and only the peer list is taken;
  - a context with a list resolves nothing;
  - no organisation gives the user alone;
  - `'system'` and `'inherit'` resolve nothing, and the user-less refusal holds;
  - a resolver failure keeps the unseeded pin and warns once.
- **Moved pin, one:** `'user' DE-ELEVATES` read `engine.seen[0]`, which is now the resolver's first read. It now reads the hook's own `update` and still asserts `isSystem: false` and `userId`. Swept for kin: `runtime/src/sandbox/hook-run-as.integration.test.ts` pins only the user-less refusal for `'user'`, which does not move. Every other `runAs` test outside these files pins flows or `'system'`.
- The real-stack probe above (5 cases).

## Ablation (committed first, mutated through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`)

- **Mutation:** the seed (`withUserGrantsSeeded` at `e82725a18`; `[SEED_USER_GRANTS]` from `f094a9d49`, re-ablated in fix round 1) returns `this` unconditionally. The marker was proved in `dist/` by `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`, in 4 built files.
- **Integration:** 2 red, the rest green:
  - `expected [ 'usr_me' ] to deeply equal [ 'usr_me', 'usr_peer' ]` (the card's shape);
  - `expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'usr_me' ]` (approvals' envelope).
  - The control and no-organisation cases stay green.
- **Unit:** 4 red: the hand-built, verbatim, no-organisation and resolver-failure pins.
- **Restore:** blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, marker `--absent` from all 14 built files. 5/5 and 20/20 green again.

## Tests and gates (head `e82725a18`, which merges `origin/main` at `3ae0b777d`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`, debt held).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck`: exit 0.
- Both packages rebuilt after the merge.
- objectql: the 49 test files that reach `ScopedContext`, the hook wrappers, `runAs` or `ctx.api`: 49 passed, 860 tests.
  - The full objectql suite does not fit the container's 10-minute foreground cap (killed at 580 s). This narrowing is declared; `Test Core` runs the full suite.
- service-automation `runas-*` and `crud-runas`: 6 files, 55 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test:repo`: 6 files, 82 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test:repo`: 1 file, 5 tests passed.
- Census rows: none owed. The `[#22661]` census keys on `referenceTargetOf` and `federated-injected-column-readers` keys on injected-column seams; this diff calls neither. Both pass.
- **Derived gates** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, no paths, 72 commands): all 72 exit 0.
  - `check:system-context-census` first went red on a new elevation read in the seed method. The read was removed (`e82725a18`), not added as a census row.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`). After a full `turbo run build`, it exited 0.
  - `--ran`: `72 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The approvals writes still see only the acting user's own row.** The status mirror (`mirrorStatusField`) deliberately carries no `tenantId`, and `approval-node.ts` carries `organizationId`, which is not an envelope field, rather than `tenantId`. Either way the seeded list is the organisation-less one, the user alone, as the table shows.
  - What moves for them today is that the list exists. Under #24341's one-policy default (`id == current_user.id || id in current_user.org_user_ids`), such a hook keeps its own row instead of losing it.
  - Seeing peers would need the producer to name the organisation it acts in. That is a `plugin-approvals` producer change (`domain:services`), not made here, and not by reading `organizationId` as an alias.
- **Positions and permission sets.** A hand-built context with no `permissions` now takes the user's resolved grants. Today such a hook falls back to the security plugin's member baseline, the #3356 gap flows closed. The approvals' envelope carries `positions: []` and `permissions: []`, which stay verbatim by the same rule that keeps a narrowed ceiling, so those hooks keep the baseline. A separate gap, on the producer.
- **Not carried into the hook's pin, as on the flow side:** `systemPermissions`, `accessible_org_ids` and `posture`. Read-only, not probed.
- **Public surface:** no nameable member is added to `ScopedContext`. The seed is keyed on a module symbol (`SEED_USER_GRANTS`) that the package entry does not export; the built `.d.ts` was checked (fix round 1, report 6266560805). No new index symbol and no spec key: `Clause-②: no`.
